speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a psychiatric condition and have noticed a new movement disorder; to help you, I need to start by asking: What specific psychiatric condition are you being treated for, and when did you first notice the movement changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent news regarding your schizophrenia symptoms. However, to determine if your new movement issues are a side effect of the risperidone or something else, can you describe exactly what movements you are experiencing and whether they happen when you are at rest or during voluntary action?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia (secondary to Risperidone).

The symptoms of inner restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of the risperidone you started. The mention of "pneumonia" in your notes appears to be inconsistent with these specific movement symptoms; did your doctor mention any lung issues or shortness of breath?
